pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered around customisation and injury-proofing — 'we want to create a resilient body that's going to last the next 10, 15, 20 years for you well, well, well into the future.' The prospect volunteered strong agreement twice and tied it directly to his own goal: 'Perfect. That's what I'm looking for' and then 'that's exactly what I'm looking for. You know, I want to be able to surf well into my 80s. And if I can do that, you know, awesome. I mean, it's, it's a perfect fit.' He then asked two good buying questions the rep answered thinly — 'How many, how many guys like my age do you have signing up?' and 'Is it harder for somebody my age to get results quick?'

Pitched on portability and sustainability, which was well aimed at a man who travels four months a year — 'if you're out traveling, you're in El Salvador, you know, I think you said Northern Spain or wherever the heck you are, like, know exactly how to eat.' The prospect responded by connecting it to his own why rather than to the food: 'that's what I want. I mean, I want to be able to enjoy, I mean, surfing is a passion of mine. And to be able to do that as long as I can, you know, for the next 20 years would be amazing.' He had already conceded the gap himself in baseline — 'I don't really have anything structured that I follow' — which is why this pillar landed most cleanly.

Delivered fully, including the form-check mechanism aimed squarely at his injury fear — 'I know you mentioned a big concern of yours is making sure we're not injured. Well, that's where this comes in. Like he's literally working with you until you have form to a T.' The rep also ran the will-you-actually-use-it check and got a clean 'Oh yeah.' The prospect agreed and generalised rather than reacting to the mechanics: 'part of this whole new lifestyle for me is surrounding myself with the kind of people that are going to promote, you know, my goals as well.' Notable that the community framing — 'they've had successful careers. You know, they're not just bums sitting on the couch' — was aimed at a retired delivery driver and drew no reaction either way.

anchors.raw: Okay. For six months. So about a thousand a month. Yeah. Okay. Wow. That's, yeah. I was thinking it was probably going to be there, but I wasn't sure. Yeah. That's a big investment.
anchors.note: He had already estimated roughly this number before it was quoted, which is the second time in this batch a prospect pre-framed $6,000 accurately. But note what he did with it: he immediately converted it to a monthly figure out loud and said 'Wow.' The per-month reframe was the prospect's own and it made the number feel larger against a fixed income, not smaller. The rep did not pick that up and never used the monthly framing deliberately.

anchors.raw: I just ordered a new board as well. That was 2200, custom.
anchors.note: Reads both ways and the rep used neither. It undercuts because it is a live claim on the same discretionary pot alongside El Salvador, Spain, Colorado and possible Barcelona and Sardinia trips. It also proves he will spend four figures on his surfing without hesitation, which is the exact argument for a programme sold as protecting his ability to surf into his eighties. A $2,200 board is useless to a man whose knees or heart stop him paddling out, and nobody made that connection.

anchors.raw: I'm on a fixed income now.
anchors.note: Volunteered unprompted at the moment of the commitment check, before the price was even said, which made it a pre-emptive frame rather than a reaction. The underlying picture is nominal comfort with unclear liquidity: a UPS pension he lived on while still saving, social security that has just started paying, and a 401k. He would not quantify any of it — 'I really don't look at it that way' — so the anchor stayed unpriced for the whole call.

anchors.raw: He's seven years older than I am. And I just got to keep up with him. You know, there's a little competitiveness there. So if I can get an edge, sure, I'll take it.
anchors.note: Dan, 71, retired UPS, does 34 strict pull-ups in a row, surfs and travels with him — and manages his 401k. The single strongest emotional lever available on this call and it was left as banter. It is also a commercial risk in the other direction: the person the prospect said he would 'go back and talk to' about the money is the same person whose physical performance is the benchmark, which makes Dan an unmanaged third party in the decision that the rep never asked a single question about.

unmet_demand.want: A way to train while travelling four and a half months a year. Named twice as the reason nothing has stuck and explicitly as what delayed this decision: 'you can't carry kettlebells with you, or, you know, so... four and a half months in about a 12-month span, you know, on the road, traveling, it's difficult to work out and keep a set routine. So that's delayed my decision a little bit.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never addressed for training. The rep applied travel to the nutrition pillar only — 'if you're out traveling, you're in El Salvador... know exactly how to eat' — and said nothing about what a kettlebell programme looks like on a surf trip to El Salvador or three weeks in Spain. The programme almost certainly has bodyweight or travel-variant answers and Trevor customises around lifestyle, so this is very likely solvable and simply went unsaid. It is the highest-value miss on the call because it was simultaneously the root cause, the timing objection and the budget conflict.

unmet_demand.want: Programming that accounts for a cardiac history. He disclosed surgically treated AFib and SVT with residual arrhythmia around 2% of the time.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Not acknowledged at all. The rep's only response was to accept the prospect's own reassurance — 'it's not debilitating. Doesn't affect working out. Okay, cool' — and later to characterise the whole medical picture as 'nothing really to worry about'. Whether the programme screens for, adapts to or requires clearance for arrhythmia is unknown from this call, which is why this is unvalidated rather than a gap. It is also the subject of a critical integrity flag.

unmet_demand.want: A straight answer on whether results come more slowly at 63 and what changes nutritionally with age. He asked directly: 'Is it harder for somebody my age to get results quick? I always hear, you know, you need more protein, you need more of this when you're, when you get older.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered with flattery instead of content — 'I wouldn't have guessed you were 64 unless you told, to be honest. I probably would have guessed, like, early 50s' — followed by a general reassurance. The protein question, which is a genuine and well-founded concern for a man in his sixties, was not answered at all. A specific, technical answer here would have been strong differentiation and instead the moment was spent on a compliment.

unmet_demand.want: Surf-specific core and hip strength. He was unusually precise about it — 'I think it's important to have a good, strong core when you're surfing. So that's one of my goals is to improve my core strength, which would include the hips' — and unusually clear that aesthetics were not the point: 'All I care about is performance, you know, what I can do when I'm out there.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep converted a performance request into an aesthetic pitch and repeated it four times: 'dropping 10% body fat in six months', 'shred the core a little bit', 'we've had guys get six packs in six months very regularly', 'Six months, six months, you get a six pack.' Nothing was said about hip mobility for paddling or pop-up, rotational core work, or transfer to time in the water. The programme plausibly delivers all of it; the pitch was aimed at a goal the prospect had explicitly disclaimed.
